title: Route / (login page) renders with no <main> landmark, breaking WCAG 1.3.1 screen-reader navigation
description: The route at http://localhost:3100/ renders the EcoExpense login/welcome page ('Welcome to EcoExpense' heading with 'Sign in' and 'sign up' buttons) inside a plain <div> with no <main> element and no role="main" anywhere in the document. This violates WCAG 1.3.1 (level A). Screen-reader users have no 'main content' landmark to skip to, so the primary content of the page is not exposed as a navigable region. The page is not a splash or loader - it is the final, fully rendered unauthenticated landing view.
expected_behavior: The fully rendered login page at route / should expose a <main> landmark (or an element with role="main") wrapping the primary content, so assistive-tech users can navigate directly to the main content region per WCAG 1.3.1 (level A).
actual_behavior: At frame Point:8 (~7980ms), the page 'Login | EcoExpense' is fully rendered (welcome heading and Sign in / sign up buttons visible) but document.querySelectorAll('main, [role=main], header, nav, footer, aside, [role=banner], [role=navigation], [role=contentinfo], [role=complementary]') returns zero elements - the DOM contains no landmarks at all.

judge_assessment.assessment:
Requirements: This report describes a missing `<main>` landmark on the route's fully rendered page, which the guidelines explicitly list as a fileable accessibility bug under the `landmark-main` check. The issue is a real WCAG 1.3.1 level A structural problem for assistive-technology users, meeting the medium severity ceiling for accessibility findings. The report also preempts the common false-positive concern by confirming the page is the final rendered login view, not a transient splash or loading state, and shows that no other landmark element compensates. Nothing in the report suggests noise, a duplicate, or an out-of-scope issue, and evidence quality is out of scope for this phase.

Evidence: The report successfully identifies a valid accessibility bug: the login page renders without a main landmark, which is confirmed by DOM querying and source inspection. The title and description correctly localize the defect to the LoginPage component. However, the report contains a critical fabrication in the root_cause.text field. It claims 'lines 13-19' is the 'loading branch'. A careful cross-reference of the provided ReadSource evidence (params/line 38) shows the loading branch is actually lines 13-19 (`if (loading) ... return ...`). While the line numbers are present, the text explicitly links the line numbers 35-60 (unauthenticated branch) to 13-19 (loading branch) by implication, creating a contradiction. Specifically, the text says: 'the loading branch (lines 13-19) is separate', implying 13-19 is loading, but the report is titled/focused on the missing main in the unauthenticated branch (35-60). The text actually gets the line numbers correct: 'lines 35-60' (unauthenticated) and 'lines 13-19' (loading). The root cause text is actually correct in its line references. Let me re-read. 'The LoginPage component ... renders its unauthenticated content (lines 35-60) ... The loading branch (lines 13-19) is separate...'. This is accurate against the ReadSource result. There are no fabricated claims. The Evaluate result confirms zero landmarks. The ReadSource confirms the div usage. All guidelines met.
